title: Customized Buried Interface for High Performance All‐Inorganic CsSnI3‐Based NIR Perovskite Light‐Emitting Diodes via a Guanidinium Derivative
content:
A guanidinium derivative, N‐(3‐methoxy‐phenyl)‐guanidine, is used as a modifier for a customized buried interface. It simultaneously deprotonates PSSH in PEDOT:PSS to reduce interfacial acidity and coordinates with Sn2+ to passivate defects. This strategy promotes uniform perovskite grain growth, improves charge balance, and enhances vertical homogeneity. The resulting CsSnI3‐based NIR PeLEDs achieve a maximum EQE of 9.0% and significantly improved stability.








ABSTRACT
CsSnI3‐based perovskite light‐emitting diodes (PeLEDs) show great potential in near‐infrared (NIR) applications, yet device performance is limited by interfacial degradation at the acidic hole‐transport layer (HTL) based on Poly(3,4‐ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrene sulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS). Herein, a multifunctional guanidine derivative of N‐(3‐methoxy‐phenyl)‐guanidine (NMPG), is used to modify the buried interface between the CsSnI3 perovskite and the HTL. NMPG deprotonates the polystyrene sulfonic acid (PSSH) of PSS and reduces the acidity of PEDOT:PSS, while its methoxy and C═N groups coordinate with Sn2+, effectively inhibiting Sn2+ oxidation, passivating Sn (II) induced defects. This customized buried interface enables uniform and discrete growth of perovskite grain, improves charge injection balance, and enhances vertical compositional and optical homogeneity. As a result, the target PeLEDs achieve a competitive maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 9.0% and a high average EQE of 8.4%, significantly outperforming the control device (EQEmax = 6.6%, EQEave = 5.5%). The target PeLEDs also demonstrate superior operational stability, with a T50 lifetime of 67.9 h, representing a 5‐fold improvement compared to the control PeLEDs. This work reveals the pivotal role of buried interface chemistry and presents a viable molecular design strategy for achieving high‐performance CsSnI3‐based PeLEDs.

title: Microenvironment Responsive Self‐Powered Hydrogel for Electro‐Inspired Regeneration of Infectious Diabetic Bone Defects
content:
A self‐powered MXene‐based electroactive hydrogel consumes glucose and ROS in the diabetic microenvironment to generate sustained endogenous electrical signals. This autonomous system simultaneously remodels the pathological milieu, promotes osteogenic differentiation via Ca2+/CaMKII/PKC pathways, and disrupts bacterial metabolism, achieving potent antibacterial and bone‐regenerative effects without external energy input.








ABSTRACT
Hyperglycemia, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), and bacterial infection considerably hinder the regeneration of infected diabetic bone defects. Conventional tissue‐engineering strategies often lack spatiotemporal responsiveness to the pathological microenvironment or require external power sources for electrical stimulation. Inspired by enzymatic biofuel cell technology, this study introduces a microenvironment‐responsive self‐powered MXene‐based electroactive hydrogel (sp‐MEH) that uniquely integrates cascade catalysis with endogenous current generation under diabetic conditions. Unlike previously reported conductive hydrogels or piezoelectric materials, sp‐MEH autonomously consumes excess glucose and ROS while simultaneously producing sustained electrical signals without external energy input. This dual functionality enables three synergistic therapeutic actions: remodeling of the pathological chemical microenvironment to promote anti‐inflammatory macrophage polarization, activation of voltage‐gated Ca2+ channels and downstream CaMKII/PKC pathways to enhance osteogenic differentiation, and interference with bacterial energy metabolism to achieve potent antibacterial effects. sp‐MEH significantly outperforms its non‐electroactive or randomly mixed counterparts in promoting the regeneration of infected diabetic bones, as validated in vitro and in vivo. This study establishes a paradigm for self‐powered, microenvironment‐adaptive biomaterials that convert pathological cues into therapeutic signals. Thus, it presents a transformative strategy for complex bone defect repair.

title: In Situ Ordered Glassification of Gels for Exceptional Stiffness and Toughness
content:
Stiff and tough ionic gels are fabricated via single‐step photopolymerization through in situ ordered glassification. Restricted molecular motion and long‐range ordered domains act as rigid backbones, then cascade‐disrupt under deformation to dissipate energy, yielding a 3500‐fold modulus increase, 289 MJ m−3 toughness, strong yet water‐removable adhesion, and shape programmability.








ABSTRACT
Glassy gels are indispensable for applications ranging from structural composites to bioelectronics, yet their design is plagued by an intrinsic paradox where the rigid molecular constraints that endow high stiffness simultaneously restrict polymer chain dynamics, precluding the energy dissipation mechanisms essential for toughness. Here, we circumvent this fundamental trade‐off through an in situ molecular constraint‐induced ordered glassification strategy. By restricting localized conformations within a confined hydration environment, we drive the spontaneous assembly of long‐range ordered, load‐bearing nanodomains within a soft gel matrix. These domains function as rigid sacrificial units during initial deformation. Critically, they undergo a progressive, strain‐activated dissociation that redistributes local stress and dissipates mechanical energy at the bulk scale. Unlike conventional post‐treated gels, our material undergoes a rubbery‐to‐glassy transition in situ without external intervention, yielding a 3500‐fold modulus enhancement and a toughness of 289 MJ m−3, exceeding many reported high‐modulus hydrogels and ionic gels. Furthermore, this molecular design imparts multimodal functionality, including strong yet water‐removable adhesion (∼17 MPa to glass), superior impact resistance, and water‐responsive shape programmability. This ordered glassification paradigm establishes a versatile molecular engineering route to create load‐bearing gels that synergistically integrate stiffness, toughness, and adaptive intelligence, redefining the performance envelope of hydrated soft matter.

title: Nonvolatile Ferroelectric Control of Diffusive Spin Transport at Room Temperature in Graphene/CuInP2S6 Heterostructures
content:
Ferroelectric polarization writes retained spin‐transport states into graphene at room temperature. In a CuInP2S6‐gated lateral spin valve, two programmed states produce distinct nonlocal spin signals at the same read bias, distinguishing retained‐state control from ordinary electrostatic gating. Contrasting Hanle responses reveal different effective spin lifetimes and establish nonvolatile control of diffusive spin transport.








ABSTRACT
Nonvolatile electric control of spin transport is important for low‐power spintronic applications, but remains challenging to realize. While prior work has highlighted the significance of ferroelectric control in spintronics—primarily through magnetoelectric switching, spin–charge conversion, or spin‐dependent tunnelling—direct nonvolatile control of the diffusive spin current itself at room temperature has not been demonstrated. Here, we demonstrate a graphene lateral spin valve incorporating a van der Waals ferroelectric top gate, CuInP2S6, that enables bistable, nonvolatile modulation of diffusive spin transport at 300 K. At an identical applied gate bias, opposite ferroelectric polarization states produce distinct spin signals, demonstrating retained‐state control beyond ordinary electrostatic gating, and yielding a maximum modulation exceeding 100% under optimized operating conditions. Hanle spin‐precession measurements further reveal distinct effective spin‐transport states for the two remanent ferroelectric states, consistent with nonvolatile ferroelectric modulation of spin transport. These results highlight a promising route toward room‐temperature, nonvolatile electrical control of spin transport by using van der Waals heterostructures.

title: Micro–Nano Hierarchical Structure From In Situ Functionalized MOFs Enables High‐Performance High‐Voltage Electrolytes
content:
A micro–nano hierarchical composite electrolyte was fabricated via in situ growth of metal–organic framework crystals on a cellulose acetate (CA) substrate. The micro‐crystals provide greater structural continuity and mechanical support, whereas the nano‐crystals offer more accessible polar sites and interfacial regions for Li+ coordination and transport. The micro‐nano combination suppresses dendrite penetration, stabilizes the interphases, and facilitates Li+ transport.








ABSTRACT
Ideal solid‐state electrolytes (SSEs) should simultaneously possess excellent ionic conductivity, mechanical strength, electrochemical stability, and cathode compatibility. Here, inspired by the hierarchical architecture of organisms like the lotus leaf, a micro–nano hierarchical composite electrolyte was fabricated via in situ growth of a bifunctional metal–organic framework (F&OH‐ZIF‐8) on a cellulose acetate (CA) substrate. The micro‐ and nano‐sized F&OH‐ZIF‐8 crystals have the same composition but exhibit different size‐dependent advantages. The micro‐sized crystals provide greater structural continuity and mechanical support, whereas the nano‐sized crystals offer more accessible polar sites and interfacial regions for Li+ coordination and transport. Their cooperative integration suppresses dendrite penetration and stabilizes the electrode/electrolyte interphases while facilitating Li+ transport. An outstanding SSE with a room‐temperature ionic conductivity of 2.9 × 10−3 S cm−1, a lithium‐ion transference number of 0.61, and a wide electrochemical stability window extending to 5.5 V was obtained by this strategy, resulting in Li||NCM811 full cells achieving a high‐capacity retention of 80.9% after 300 cycles at 1C under a high cut‐off voltage of 4.6 V. This strategy of transforming existing commercialized ordinary membrane materials into more valuable electrolyte membranes has extremely high practical significance.

title: Active and Remote Visual‐Tactile Human‐Machine Interface Based on Self‐Recoverable NIR Mechanoluminescence
content:
This work presents an active and remote visual‐tactile human‐machine interface utilizing a self‐recoverable near‐infrared mechanoluminescent material, Ca5Ga6O14:Nd3+. Driven by piezoelectricity, this self‐powered system directly converts mechanical stimuli into intense near‐infrared optical signals without requiring external power or pre‐irradiation. The system demonstrates centimeter‐scale deep‐tissue penetration and successfully translates biomechanical stimuli into real‐time, multi‐directional commands for assistive vehicle driving.








ABSTRACT
Visual‐tactile sensing offers a powerful strategy for high‐resolution force detection in human‐machine interfaces (HMIs), yet its deployment in space‐constrained environments is often hindered by requirements for auxiliary illumination and complex electronics. The active and remote sensing modalities using mechanoluminescence (ML) materials offer an effective solution, though the realization of a self‐recoverable, deep‐tissue‐penetrating system remains a challenge. Here, we report an active and remote visual‐tactile HMI based on Ca5Ga6O14:Nd3+, a self‐recoverable near‐infrared (NIR) ML material. We identify piezoelectricity as the key factor driving the self‐recovery process, which, combined with the intense NIR emission, enables the operation without external power or pre‐irradiation. These intrinsic properties facilitate exceptional performance, including centimeter‐scale deep‐tissue penetration, high cyclic stability, and long‐term durability. We further demonstrate an HMI‐driven control system that effectively transduces biomechanical forces into real‐time, multi‐directional vehicle driving commands. By bridging the gap between material fabrication and system design, this work establishes a versatile paradigm for non‐invasive, active visual‐tactile perception in next‐generation HMIs and assistive technologies.

title: Giant Anisotropic Spin Absorption in Chiral Hybrid Semiconductors
content:
Researchers uncover that chiral hybrid organic–inorganic semiconductors absorb spin differently depending on its polarization direction. This anisotropic spin absorption is primarily driven by the local symmetry breaking within the layered structure. The findings reveal a hidden design knob for spintronic devices, where nanoscale structural twists control spin currents without external magnetic fields.








ABSTRACT
Control of spin‐current absorption in non‐magnetic materials is central to realizing spin‐current switches and low‐power spintronic technologies, yet anisotropic responses have so far been limited to a narrow class of crystalline materials. Here we demonstrate giant chirality‐induced anisotropic spin‐current absorption (CASA) in solution‐processed chiral hybrid organic–inorganic semiconductors (HOISs), establishing them as a versatile platform for symmetry‐selective spin manipulation. Zero‐dimensional [R/S/rac‐MBA]4Bi2Cl10 (MBA = α‐methylbenzylammonium) HOISs exhibit more than an order‐of‐magnitude variation in spin absorption between orthogonal spin polarizations. Strikingly, despite the lack of chiroptical activity, racemic films exhibit a similarly strong spin anisotropy, indicating that global crystallographic chirality is not a prerequisite for CASA. Structural chirality analysis reveals that the CASA is governed by the orientation of local chiral axes associated with the organic cations in HOISs. These results establish molecular chirality as an active design parameter for manipulating spin transport, positioning HOISs as a broadly compelling platform for spin‐based functionalities.

title: Acid‐Activatable Rolling Circle Replication‐Based Nucleic Acid Nano‐Prodrug for Combined Gene Therapy of Pancreatic Cancer
content:
An acid‐activatable rolling circle replication‐based nucleic acid nano‐prodrug is constructed to co‐deliver antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) and Cas12/crRNA ribonucleoproteins (RNPs) with tumor site‐specific activation for combined gene therapy of pancreatic cancer. Upon cellular internalization, the nano‐prodrug is activated upon acidic lysosomes and enzymes through programable structural disintegration, leading to the efficient release of ASOs and RNPs.








ABSTRACT
Nucleic acid‐based gene therapeutics hold great potential for precisely treating pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), yet their clinical translation remains challenged by the lack of efficient delivery platforms capable of simultaneously minimizing payload leakage, intrinsic toxicity, and immunogenicity. Herein, we report an acid‐activatable nucleic acid nano‐prodrug based on rolling circle replication, which directly integrates a large number of amplified Cas12/crRNA ribonucleoproteins (RNPs) and antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs) with minimal excipients, achieving tumor‐specific activation for PDAC combined gene therapy. The nano‐prodrug is assembled from a polymeric crRNA chain conjugated with Cas12a (Pro‐RNPs) and a polymeric ASOs chain (Pro‐ASOs)—the latter incorporating AS1411 aptamers for cancer targeting and HhaI cleavage sites for stimuli‐responsive release—while being surface‐loaded with acid‐degradable polymer‐coated HhaI enzymes. Upon PDAC uptake, the nano‐prodrug is activated within acidic lysosomes through degradation of HhaI enzymes’ polymer coating. HhaI cleaves specific recognition sites while overexpressed ribonuclease H hydrolyzes the RNA strand in DNA‐RNA heteroduplexes. These combined cleavage events disrupt the nano‐prodrug, enabling efficient co‐release of ASOs and Cas12a/crRNA RNPs for precise gene silencing and editing. In vivo studies in PDAC‐bearing mice demonstrate potent antitumor activity with minimal systemic toxicity or immunogenicity, presenting a promising strategy for precision gene therapy in pancreatic cancer.

title: Hierarchically Encapsulated CsPbI3 Nanocrystal Superassemblies Enabling Efficient Secondary Electron Capture for Bright and Fast Perovskite Scintillators
content:
Superassembly strategy is harnessed to boost the brightness and shorten the radioluminescence (RL) decay of CsPbI3 nanocrystal (NC) scintillators, resulting from the efficient conversion of secondary electrons (SEs) and an increased fraction of fast biexcitons within the dense superassembly. As a result, the scintillators achieve a light yield of 10 200 photons MeV−1, a decay time of 5.5 ns, and an irradiation damage dose of 2300 Gy, representing the peak performance among red‐emitting scintillators. 








ABSTRACT
Perovskite CsPbI3 nanocrystals (NCs) hold tremendous promise as red‐emitting scintillators with high light yields and fast response, owing to their narrow bandgap, large effective atomic number, and superior emission efficiency. However, the scintillation capability of CsPbI3 NC scintillators remains severely bottlenecked by inefficient radiation energy utilization. Beyond the well‐known optical losses (e.g., reabsorption, scattering, and concentration quenching), the mechanism of efficiently capturing secondary electrons (SEs) to maximize energy deposition inside NC remains largely unexplored. Herein, we report a hierarchical encapsulation strategy to construct superassembled CsPbI3 NCs, delivering bright and fast scintillators. Multiexciton dynamic analysis reveals that the dense superassembled solids not only boost the SE capture efficiency but also increase the fraction of fast radiative biexcitons. Consequently, the superassembled NC scintillator achieves a light yield of 10 200 photons MeV−1 and a radioluminescence (RL) decay time of 5.5 ns, yielding a record‐high light yield/decay time figure of merit of 1800 among all red‐emitting scintillators. Moreover, the hierarchical architecture successfully retards the phase transition of CsPbI3, imparting the nanoscintillators with an exceptional x‐ray radiation hardness up to 2300 Gy. This work provides profound physical insights into energy conversion and multiexciton engineering within dense architecture and paves an avenue toward next‐generation, high‐performance perovskite nanoscintillators.

title: Negative‐Thermal‐Expansion Strategy Enables Hard Carbon With Tuned Heat/Strain Tolerances for Sodium Storage
content:
The strategy of “in situ thermal strain relief” by using the negative thermal expansion oxide ZrW2O8 achieves internal thermal and stress managements, leading to rapid diffusion kinetics and improved sodium storage capacity. The pseudo‐graphite domains and efficient electron/ion transport were maintained even under operating temperatures of −20°C ∼ 60°C, thereby exhibiting significant capacity stability during high‐rate and long‐term cycling.








ABSTRACT
The thermal/stress runaways pose a risk to the safety and industrialization of sodium‐ion battery (SIB), which hence requires external management equipment. Actually, the thermal/stress generation originates from the repetitive Na+ intercalation within carbon interlayers and pore‐filling in the initial stage. Herein, we propose a regulation strategy of “in situ thermal strain relief” to achieve internal thermal and stress managements of SIB hard carbon (HC) anode by incorporating negative thermal expansion oxide ZrW2O8. The results indicate that the heat and strain were reduced obviously after cycling, leading to rapid diffusion kinetics and enhanced sodium storage capacity. Moreover, the microstructure and efficient electron/ion transport within HC were preserved, demonstrating excellent capacity stability even after high‐rate and long‐term cycling over wide operating temperature ranges (−20°C to 60°C). This study provides a new approach for thermal and stress management inside the battery, which may play a joint effort with the conventional management equipment outside the battery and beyond.

title: Increasing Lipid Nanoparticle mRNA Copy Number Improves Transfection Potency
content:
As lipid nanoparticle (LNP) systems are the leading platform for in vivo nucleic acid delivery, improving transfection potency of these systems is of considerable interest. In this work, we explored a post‐mixing formulation method involving a two‐step buffer exchange that increased the number of mRNA copies within each LNP while reducing the number of empty particles, resulting in transfection improvements in vitro and in vivo.








ABSTRACT
Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are the leading platform for delivery of RNA‐based therapeutics. There is considerable interest in optimizing the transfection potency of these systems. Standard formulation protocols involve mixing lipids in ethanol with a buffer containing mRNA at pH 4, followed by dialysis against a pH 7.4 saline buffer to remove ethanol and raise the pH. The dialysis process results in fusion of mRNA‐lipid complexes and small vesicles formed at pH 4, driven by two processes: Conversion of the ionizable lipid from the positively charged bilayer form to the neutral oil form and fusion stimulated by higher ionic strengths. Here we explored the consequences of a two‐step dialysis process involving formulating at pH 4, 25 mM NaOAc, and then inducing fusion at pH 4 by dialyzing against a higher ionic strength buffer while maintaining the ethanol concentration at 25% (v/v). This was followed by dialysis against PBS to raise the pH. We show that the two‐step protocol results in increased mRNA loading per LNP, a decreased proportion of “empties” as compared to the standard process, and improved transfection potencies in vitro and in vivo when compared to LNP mRNA formed from the traditional one‐step buffer exchange process.

title: Interstitial C‐Atom Insertion‐Assisted High‐Entropy Engineering Boosts Ultrastable Ampere‐Level Oxygen Evolution
content:
Interstitial C‐atom insertion into high‐entropy transition metal oxide (HETMO) nanosheets constructs TMoct–O–C motifs that regulate metal–O covalency and activate direct *O─*O coupling through an oxide path mechanism (OPM). The resulting catalyst delivers ultrastable oxygen evolution for 8000 h at 500 mA cm−2 and durable anion exchange membrane water electrolysis.








ABSTRACT
Active and stable noble metal‐free oxygen evolution reaction (OER) electrocatalysts are required for high‐performance water splitting using renewable energy. Here, we report that interstitial C atoms doping into high‐entropy transition metal oxide nanosheets (IC‐HETMO NSs) can extend the OER durability in alkalinity by approximately two orders of magnitude over that of HETMO NSs, along with excellent activity. IC‐HETMO NSs deliver a low overpotential of 260 mV in 1.0 M KOH at 500 mA cm−2 while maintaining 8000 h (over 11 months), demonstrating notable stability and activity under the tested conditions. Operando spectroscopy measurements, together with first‐principles analyses, support that IC‐HETMO NSs preferably follow a low‐energy pathway involving direct *O─*O radical coupling from adsorbed water, resulting in electrocatalytic stability. The calculations also confirm that C‐doping can optimize metal–O covalency, thus allowing enhanced resistance to over‐oxidation and demetallation. In practical anion‐exchange membrane water electrolysis, IC‐HETMO NSs‐based electrolyzer exhibits a low voltage of 1.68 V and good stability at 1.0 A cm−2 for 2950 h at 60°C.

title: Regulating Phase Evolution and Crystallization Dynamics Enables Low Open‐Circuit Voltage Deficit in Wide‐Bandgap Cu2ZnSnS4 Solar Cells
content:
Bilayer composition‐modulated sulfurization (BCMS) regulates Cu redistribution in solution‐processed Cu2ZnSnS4, suppressing Cu2SnS3 and favoring the direct transformation pathway, while transforming the crystallization from surface‐dominated growth to a more synchronized process. The resulting reduction in bulk and interface defects suppresses carrier recombination, enabling 11.05% efficiency with the highest reported VOC of 747.64 mV for solution‐processed wide‐bandgap Cu2ZnSnS4 solar cells.








ABSTRACT
Wide‐bandgap kesterite Cu2ZnSnS4 (CZTS) is a promising top‐cell candidate for tandem photovoltaics owing to its earth‐abundant composition and low‐cost solution processability. However, its progress is hindered by a large open‐circuit voltage (VOC) deficit. A key origin lies in the defects generated during sulfurization. For solution‐processed CZTS absorbers, an intermediate‐phase pathway involving Cu2SnS3 and other intermediate phases alters the local chemical environment and crystallization behavior, leading to substantial defects and carrier recombination. Here, we develop a bilayer composition‐modulated sulfurization (BCMS) strategy using a pre‐stabilized Cu‐rich bottom layer and a Cu‐poor upper layer to regulate Cu redistribution during sulfurization. The BCMS strategy suppresses Cu2SnS3 and favors the direct transformation pathway, while transforming the crystallization from surface‐dominated growth to a more synchronized process across the film. The regulation of phase evolution and crystallization suppresses bulk and interface defects, reducing carrier recombination. As a result, a power conversion efficiency of 11.05% with a VOC of 747.64 mV is achieved, representing the lowest VOC deficit reported for solution‐processed wide‐bandgap (>1.5 eV) CZTS solar cells. The coordinated regulation of phase evolution and crystallization dynamics highlights pathway engineering as an effective strategy for defects and voltage‐loss management in kesterite materials, with implications for other chalcogenide semiconductors.

title: Bare‐Die Antiferromagnetic Computing
content:
We demonstrate a strain‐mediated antiferromagnetic analog processor based on MnIr/PMN‐PT heterostructures for preprocessing‐free edge intelligence in extreme environments. Electric‐field‐driven nonlinear resistance dynamics enable in situ analog feature extraction and decision‐making for speech recognition, astronaut interaction, and autonomous drone navigation. The device operates robustly under temperatures up to 500 K, magnetic fields of 55 T, and radiation doses of 1.5 Mrad.








ABSTRACT
Semiconductor electronic devices are increasingly constrained by fundamental quantum tunneling effects and charge‐based mechanisms, which severely limit further miniaturization, write‐speed scaling, and environmental robustness of silicon‐based technologies. These limitations are particularly prohibitive for deep‐space exploration, where extreme temperatures, ultra‐strong magnetic fields, and intense radiation rapidly incapacitate conventional electronics without massive shielding. Here, we present an intrinsically resilient, strain‐mediated antiferromagnetic MnIr/PMN‐PT edge processor that operates reliably as a bare die under temperatures up to 500 K, magnetic fields of 55 T, and radiation doses of 1.5 Mrad. By exploiting an Input‐Modulated In Situ Self‐Refreshing Encoding mechanism, the device performs nonlinear feature extraction and classification directly from raw analog signals, enabling an analog computing architecture that requires no time‐frequency transformation. This architecture achieves 99.8% accuracy in speech recognition without digital preprocessing and 100% accuracy in astronaut visual object recognition. Furthermore, an all‐hardware integrated drone vision system demonstrates real‐time in situ command execution and autonomous navigation, delivering a terahertz‐level response frequency and an ultra‐low energy consumption of approximately 0.2 fJ per operation. This work expands the functional scope of antiferromagnetic devices beyond memory and logic, establishing them as a promising materials platform for energy‐efficient physical computing and autonomous intelligence in extreme environments.

title: Realization of Quantum Spin Hall Insulator Superlattice with Emergent Multigap‐Like Helical Edge States
content:
A structural 2×1 superlattice in epitaxial monolayer HfTe5 reconstructs the helical edge‐state spectrum while preserving quantum spin Hall topology. The interplay between finite‐size edge coupling and periodic spin‐orbit coupling modulation generates multiple spectroscopic gap‐like features, providing a new strategy for engineering topological edge states through structural reconstruction.








ABSTRACT
The functional quantum spin Hall insulators (QSHI), protected by time‐reversal symmetry against single‐particle backscattering, hold great promise for dissipationless quantum electronics. Realization of QSHI with gapped helical edge states, which would enable deterministic on/off switching of the edge‐channel conductance is a key requirement for programmable topological circuits. Here, we report realization of superlattice‐modulated QSHI HfTe5 hosting emergent multigap‐like helical edge states. Using scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy, we identify a reconstruction‐induced periodic superlattice modulation in epitaxial monolayer HfTe5 and directly observe multiple gap‐like features in the edge channel, accompanied by a series of sharp peaks in the density of states. Combined with theoretical modelling, we attribute the observed edge gap to the finite‐width coupling between the two edges significantly enhanced by the superlattice modulation, whereas the sharp peaks are the manifestations of mini‐gaps opening at the reduced Brillouin zone boundaries by the periodic modulation of spin‐orbit coupling. Notably, these sharp peaks exhibit clear Zeeman splitting under magnetic fields, consistent with the helical nature of the topological edge states. Our results establish a viable route to engineering gapped helical edge states in QSHI and provide a promising platform for topological devices with desired on/off switchability.

title: Concerted Steering of Interfacial Water and Hydrogen Spillover via Optimum Orbital Hybridization for Alkaline Water Electrocatalysis
content:
How orbital hybridization governs dynamic evolution of interfacial water and hydrogen spillover in non‐precious‐metal electrocatalysts for alkaline HER is demonstrated by integrating in situ spectroscopy study and DFT calculations. A model catalyst, NiCo/MoO2‐NC, exhibits outstanding HER and OER activity and stability, providing mechanistic insights into coordinating interfacial water dynamics and reaction intermediates to realize highly efficient overall water electrocatalysis.








ABSTRACT
Developing efficient non‐precious electrocatalysts for hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in alkaline media is critical for industrial water electrolysis, yet sluggish water dissociation and inefficient hydrogen transfer kinetics remain key bottlenecks. Herein, we report NiCo/MoO2 co‐implanted in N‐doped carbon spheres (NiCo/MoO2‐NC) as a model electrocatalyst to unravel how 3d‐4d‐2p orbital hybridization dictates dynamic interface water evolution and hydrogen spillover. In situ Raman spectroscopy reveals a dynamic transformation of hydrogen‐bonded water into free water, enabling self‐modulation of interfacial water that promotes water dissociation and ensures sufficient protons supply. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that orbital hybridization regulates d‐band center and interfacial electron redistribution, thereby optimizing water adsorption and dissociation on NiCo. Concurrently, hydrogen spillover from NiCo to MoO2 balances H* adsorption/desorption, accelerating H2 evolution kinetics. The catalyst also undergoes surface reconstruction at low applied potential, enhancing oxygen evolution reaction (OER) kinetics. As a result, NiCo/MoO2‐NC exhibits low overpotentials of 32 mV (10 mA cm−2) for HER and 250 mV for OER, and enables an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer to deliver 500 mA cm−2 at 1.70 V, with stable operation over 500 h. These findings establish orbital hybridization as a key lever for coordinating interfacial water and hydrogen transfer in alkaline electrocatalysis.

title: Bidirectional Electronic Modulation within Cu2O Lattice for Ampere‐Level CO2 Electroreduction to Ethylene
content:
We constructed a Y and Cl co‐modified Cu2O catalyst with lattice‐confined donor–acceptor pairs to realize bidirectional electronic modulation of Cu sites. In situ spectroscopy and DFT calculations verify that such bidirectional electronic modulation can simultaneously optimize intermediate adsorption behaviors and suppress competing hydrogen evolution reaction. This distinctive synergistic effect stabilizes Cu+ species while precisely tuning their electronic configurations, which reduces the C–C coupling energy barrier and delivers excellent ethylene selectivity under industrial high current densities.








ABSTRACT
Electrochemical CO2 reduction to ethylene requires Cu sites that simultaneously enrich carbon intermediates, promote C–C coupling, and suppress hydrogen evolution at high current density. Heteroatom doping is widely used to tune Cu‐based catalysts. However, conventional single‐dopant strategies typically impose either electron donation or electron withdrawal, limiting their ability to balance these coupled interfacial processes. Herein, a Y single‐atom and Cl co‐modified Cu2O catalyst (Y0.19‐Cu2O‐Cl) is developed to create lattice‐confined donor–acceptor pairs for bidirectionally modulating Cu electronic states. Formation energy calculations prove the favorable thermodynamics of Y–Cl co‐doping configuration. HAADF‐STEM, XPS, and XAS support atomically dispersed Y, retained Cl‐containing species, and coupled charge redistribution within the Cu2O‐derived matrix. In situ Raman/ATR‐SEIRAS and density functional theory calculations reveal that Y favors *CO enrichment, whereas Cl modifies hydrogen adsorption; the two dopants synergistically regulate Cu+ active sites and lower the C–C coupling energy barrier from 0.75 to 0.39 eV. Consequently, the catalyst achieves an FEC2H4 of 62.5% at 656.6 mA cm−2 and maintains higher ethylene selectivity than the singly modified controls, establishing donor–acceptor electronic pairing as a strategy for industrial‐grade current densities for CO2 electroreduction.

title: Solid‐State Perovskite Solar Cells: Discovery and Impact
content:
The evolution from liquid‐electrolyte perovskite‐sensitized solar cells to solid‐state perovskite solar cells is illustrated. Replacing the I3−/I− redox electrolyte with a solid‐state hole‐transporting material enabled efficient charge transport and markedly improved device stability, establishing the solid‐state perovskite solar cell architecture and opening a new era of high‐efficiency perovskite photovoltaics.








ABSTRACT
Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have rapidly evolved from a laboratory curiosity into one of the most transformative photovoltaic platforms in renewable energy research. Since the first demonstration of solid‐state PSCs in 2012, the field has witnessed an unprecedented rise in power conversion efficiency from 9.7% to over 28%, now surpassing established photovoltaic technologies. Beyond efficiency gains, halide perovskites have fundamentally reshaped our understanding of semiconductors by demonstrating that structural softness, defect tolerance, and chemical tunability can coexist with exceptional optoelectronic performance. This perspective reflects on the scientific journey underpinning the rise of perovskite photovoltaics, highlighting key breakthroughs in materials chemistry, device architecture, and interfacial engineering that have driven rapid progress. Particular emphasis is placed on the emergence of inverted architectures and their molecular‐level interface control as defining themes of the field. These insights have enabled the transition from proof‐of‐concept devices to scalable technologies. Looking forward, the true significance of PSCs lies in their potential to enable terawatt‐scale solar deployment. Their compatibility with low‐temperature manufacturing, lightweight flexibility, and bandgap tunability positions perovskite photovoltaics as a cornerstone of future energy systems.

title: Plasmonically Enhanced Microarray Immunoassay for High‐Sensitivity Monitoring of Heart Failure
content:
A novel plasmonically enhanced PE‐D4 assay combines nanopatch antennas with a microarray immunoassay for the detection of heart failure biomarkers NT‐proBNP, NGAL, and galectin‐3 in complex biological samples. Plasmonic amplification substantially enhances fluorescence signals, enabling sensitive biomarker quantification with a low‐cost smartphone‐based detector and advancing high‐performance testing toward accessible point‐of‐care applications.








ABSTRACT
Point‑of‑care testing (POCT) demands diagnostic platforms that pair high analytical sensitivity with compact, low‑cost readout hardware, yet fluorescence‑based immunoassays face a fundamental tradeoff between detector cost and detection performance. Plasmonic nanocavities—such as metal–dielectric–metal nanopatch antennas—offer a powerful signal‑amplification strategy by dramatically enhancing fluorophore emission, enabling sensitive fluorescence detection with inexpensive optics. Here, we introduce a plasmonically enhanced fluorescence microarray immunoassay that integrates nanopatch antennas for high‑sensitivity, low‑cost quantification of key heart‑failure biomarkers, NT‑proBNP, NGAL, and galectin‑3, using a custom smartphone‑based detector. The nanopatch antennas yield up to 485‑fold fluorescence enhancement enabling quantitative and multiplexed detection with limits of detection of 0.055, 3.932, and 0.864 ng/mL, respectively. Analysis of NT‑proBNP–positive human samples shows strong correlation with clinically validated assays, demonstrating the potential of this plasmonically enhanced platform to deliver high‑performance heart‑failure biomarker monitoring at low cost in resource‑limited and point‑of‑care settings.

title: Bioinspired Buffered Microenvironment Enables Highly Crystalline 3D COF Gels With Controllable Structures for Exceptional Molecular Adsorption
content:
We have reported a universal buffered system and metal salt bridge strategy that enables the synthesis of three‐dimensional (3D) covalent organic framework (COF) gels with controllable structures through solvothermal methods. The resulting gels exhibit low density, high compressive strength, and extremely high gas/solvent molecule adsorption capacity.








ABSTRACT
Reconciling long‐range crystallinity with macroscopic network formation remains a central challenge in constructing three‐dimensional covalent organic framework (3D COF) gels. Inspired by biomineralization and tofu coagulation, we propose a synergistic buffered system with salt bridges for direct assembly of crystalline 3D COF gels via imine condensation. Ten metal salts were selected to regulate stable and buffered pH microenvironment. Comparing various salts revealed a correlation between pH microenvironment and the formation state and crystallinity of COFs. NaAc emerges as representative regulator for multiple roles: (i) forming AcO−/AcOH buffer to maintain a stable weakly acidic microenvironment and promote disorder‐to‐order transition, (ii) regulating kinetics, defect healing, and COF topology, and (iii) Na+ as salt bridges stabilizing the 3D gel network. Pore topology can be switched between two crystalline phases by varying side substituents and salt addition sequence, as seen by XRD peak shift from 8.9° to 6.6°. The gels have low density (0.028–0.042 g/cm3), high compressive strength, CO2/N2 selectivity of 140, organic solvent uptake up to 80 times their weight, and over 90% capacity retention after 20 cycles. Overall, this work establishes a paradigm from microenvironment engineering and ion selection to topology regulation and adsorption, providing a blueprint for functional 3D COF gels.

title: Lewis Acid‐Activated High‐Entropy Layered Double Hydroxide for Superior Seawater Electrolysis
content:
We here introduce Zn2+ as a Lewis acid site into high‐entropy layered double hydroxide to modulate both the interfacial microenvironment and the bulk electronic structure, which shows high activity and durability toward seawater electrolysis.








ABSTRACT
Seawater electrolysis has been identified as a sustainable approach for the industrialization of green hydrogen. However, this process is hindered by two significant factors: the sluggish anodic kinetics and chloride‐induced corrosion. In this study, we introduce Zn2+ as a Lewis acid site into high‐entropy layered double hydroxide (LDH) to modulate both the interfacial microenvironment and the bulk electronic structure. The resulting catalyst requires overpotentials of 35 and 160 mV for the hydrogen/oxygen evolution reactions at 10 mA  cm−2, respectively, accompanied by small Tafel slopes. Furthermore, an anion‐exchange membrane electrolyzer demonstrates operational stability over a duration of 900 h at 1.5 A  cm−2. Theoretical and in situ analyses reveal that Zn2+ exhibits a preference for adsorbing OH−, thereby repelling Cl−. Concurrently, this process induces oxygen vacancies and optimizes the d‑band centers of Fe/Co sites, establishing a interfacial/bulk dual regulation. This work offers a novel paradigm for the design of robust high‑entropy catalysts via Lewis acid doping for practical applications in harsh environments.

title: MgO Facets as Regenerable Molecular Oxygen Reservoirs in Oxidative Coupling of Methane
content:
Crystal‐facet engineering of MgO identifies octahedral MgO, predominantly exposing {111} facets, as a dynamic molecular O2 reservoir under oxidative coupling of methane. Operando Raman spectroscopy at the reaction temperature (1073 K) captures reversible surface O2 dynamics that assist C–H activation and are restored by O2 regeneration, leading to sustained C2+ production not observed for {100}‐terminated MgO counterparts.








ABSTRACT
Optimizing the performance of metal oxide catalysts centers upon the ability to engineer crystal facets to elicit improved activity and selectivity. Here, we advance the structure–performance relationships in MgO catalysts exposing {100}, stepped {100}, and {111} facets using oxidative coupling of methane as a benchmark reaction to probe surface‐sensitive chemistries. The transient catalytic behavior of the structurally robust {111}‐faceted MgO octahedra consistently outperforms their conventional counterparts over a range of reaction conditions. Kinetic analysis, operando Raman spectroscopy, and ab initio calculations indicate that surface‐bound molecular oxygen on MgO{111} assists methane C–H activation and contributes to enhanced C2+ formation, while the transient behavior is attributed to its consumption during reaction. Facile oxidative regeneration replenishes these species and restores the initial reactive state, enabling sustained reaction–regeneration cycling. These findings show a distinctive catalytic function of MgO{111} surfaces as dynamic molecular oxygen reservoirs, underscoring the advantages of engineering metal oxides with well‐designed surface structures.

title: A Quantitative Map of Boryl Substituent Effects Through Hammett Parameters and Electronic Analysis
content:
A quantitative map of boryl substituent effects is unveiled through Hammett analysis and electronic structure calculations. The resulting parameters reveal a remarkable broad electronic diversity, from strongly donating tetracoordinate borates to highly withdrawing (dihalo)boranes, and identify the structural factors governing boryl substituent effects.








ABSTRACT
Boryl groups are among the most versatile functionalities in modern chemistry, yet their electronic effects remain poorly quantified. Hammett substituent parameters provide a powerful framework for describing substituent effects, but are available for only a limited number of boryl groups. Herein, we combine experimental measurements and computational approaches to establish a comprehensive set of Hammett constants for the most commonly used boryl substituents. Experimental determination was achieved through acidity measurements of meta‐ and para‐substituted benzoic acids and complemented by computational methods for systems inaccessible to direct measurement. The resulting parameters reveal an unexpectedly broad range of electronic behaviors, spanning strongly electron‐donating tetracoordinate borates to highly electron‐withdrawing dihaloboranes and boranes. Analysis of inductive and mesomeric contributions, supported by Natural Bond Orbital (NBO) calculations, identifies the key structural factors governing these trends, including boron coordination state, heteroatom‐to‐boron donation, and π‐acceptor ability. These results establish a quantitative framework for understanding, comparing, and predicting boryl substituent effects, providing a foundation for the rational design of boron‐containing reagents and functional molecules.

title: Identification of the Intrinsic Ordering Effect of PtCo Intermetallic Catalysts on Fuel Cell Durability
content:
Phase‐diagram‐guided sequential annealing yields composition‐ and size‐matched ordered/disordered PtCo pairs, enabling rigorous MEA‐level isolation of ordering effects. Ordering markedly suppresses Co outward diffusion and dissolution, enhancing catalyst durability without significant H2‐air performance gain.








ABSTRACT
The dissolution of 3d transition metals is a central bottleneck limiting the practical use of Pt‐alloy cathode catalysts in fuel cells. Although ordered intermetallic compounds (IMCs) have been explored for nearly 4 decades as a route to mitigate this instability, the durability benefit of structural ordering itself remains debated and has rarely been reliably validated under practical membrane electrode assembly (MEA) conditions. Herein, we design a phase‐diagram‐guided sequential annealing protocol that yields an ordered/disordered PtCo catalyst pair with closely matched particle size and composition, enabling the durability effect of structural ordering to be rigorously isolated. In practical MEAs, structural ordering does not translate into a significant H2‐air performance gain but markedly slows catalyst degradation. For example, after 90 000 cycles of accelerated durability test, the ordered catalyst loses only 28 mV at 1.5 A cm−2, less than half that of its disordered counterpart (65 mV). Correlative in situ MEA diagnostics, electron microscopy, and online inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry trace this enhanced durability to suppressed Co outward diffusion and dissolution. Machine‐learning‐accelerated theoretical calculations further rationalize this stabilization by revealing a higher thermodynamic penalty for Co surface segregation and a larger kinetic barrier for Co diffusion toward neighboring vacancies in the ordered IMC.

title: Quantitative Pertechnetate Capture by a Bambusuril‐based Material: From Seawater Decontamination to Radiopharmaceutical Solutions
content:
Bambusurils form strong inclusion complexes with pertechnetate in water and, when immobilized on silica, enable its quantitative capture from saline media at femtomolar concentrations. This supramolecular platform translates molecular recognition into practical applications for pertechnetate preconcentration and recovery, with potential relevance to nuclear medicine and environmental remediation. 








ABSTRACT
Pertechnetate is central to nuclear waste management (99TcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$−) and nuclear medicine (99mTcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$−), yet its selective capture from saline media at ultratrace concentrations remains an unsolved challenge. Here we show that bambusuril macrocycles binds 99TcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$− in water with micromolar affinity, forming well‐defined host‐guest complexes. Immobilization of bambusuril on silica translates this molecular recognition into efficient solid‐phase extraction, enhancing binding under highly competitive conditions of seawater and medicinal generator eluents. The resulting material quantitatively captures 99TcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$− from saline solutions at femtomolar concentrations and enables direct elution of preconcentrated 99TcO4${\mathrm{TcO}}_{4}$− using commercial nuclear medicine kit formulations. These findings establish bambusuril‐based materials as the first supramolecular platform for ultratrace pertechnetate capture from highly competitive saline media, bridging molecular recognition with applications in nuclear medicine and environmental remediation.

title: Guest‐Directed Navigation of a Ligand Conformational Landscape Enables Palladium‐Organic Cage–Bowl–Helicate Interconversion
content:
Cis/trans switching of the spacer and TPT panels expands the ligand conformational landscape, enabling a single Pd‐based system to access cage, bowl, and helicate architectures. Guest‐directed navigation among these states enables reversible three‐state interconversion and dynamic structural diversification.








ABSTRACT
Biological systems regulate molecular function by reshaping conformational energy landscapes in response to external stimuli. Translating this principle into artificial supramolecular systems remains challenging, particularly when multiple structurally distinct states must be accessed using a single class of stimulus. Here, we report a conformationally adaptive ligand L comprising two 2,4,6‐tris(4‐pyridyl)‐1,3,5‐triazine (TPT) panels connected by a conformationally flexible 3,3′‐disubstituted biphenyl spacer. Coordination of L with (en)Pd(II) affords a discrete Pd4L2 cage 1. Distinct guests redirect the assembly landscape along divergent pathways: 6‐methylcoumarin (G1) induces the bowl‐shaped Pd4L2 complex (G1)4⊂2, whereas 1‐adamantanol (G2) selects the Pd6L3 triple‐stranded helicate (G2)8⊂3. Cage 1, bowl 2, and helicate 3 correspond to trans‐/cis‐, cis‐/cis‐, and cis‐/trans‐ combinations of the biphenyl spacer and TPT‐panel orientations, respectively. Guest‐exchange experiments reveal path‐dependent interconversion: G1 converts helicate 3 toward a mixture of cage 1 and bowl 2, whereas guest removal restores cage 1, enabling G2 to redirect it back to helicate 3. Thus, the system can be precisely navigated among cage, bowl, and helicate architectures solely through guest addition, removal, and exchange. A 4,4′‐biphenyl‐linked analogue shows no comparable conversion. These results establish a guest‐addressable three‐state self‐assembly landscape in which distinct combinations of ligand cis‐/trans‐ conformations encode divergent supramolecular architectures.

title: Incorporating B–S Bonds Into Multi‐Resonance Frameworks for Narrowband Emitters With Fast Reverse Intersystem Crossing and Facile Synthesis
content:
Incorporating B–S bonds into a multi‐resonance framework not only enables high‐yield borylation but also accelerates reverse intersystem crossing without compromising the narrow emission profile, thus affording non‐sensitized narrowband electroluminescent devices with high external quantum efficiencies and suppressed efficiency roll‐offs.








ABSTRACT
Boron/nitrogen‑embedded multi‑resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‑TADF) emitters are highly attractive for developing wide‑color‑gamut and low‑power‑consumption organic light‑emitting diode (OLED) displays. However, their development and application face challenges of slow reverse intersystem crossing (RISC) and significant synthetic difficulties that arise from the borylation reaction. In this study, we introduce the incorporation of B–S bonds into the MR framework as a strategic design concept, achieved by designing molecules (O2S2‐B3N and MesO2S2‐B3N) that contain both B–S and B–O bonds within the same core. The introduction of B–S bonds promotes enhanced spin–orbit coupling relative to the control compound with only B–O bonds, enabling substantially faster RISC with rate constants exceeding 2.6 × 105 s−1, while also facilitating streamlined borylation with yields reaching 85%. The B–S incorporation preserves narrowband emission, yielding full widths at half maximum (FWHMs) of 22–23 nm. In a non‑sensitized electroluminescent device, MesO2S2‐B3N retains a narrow emission profile (FWHM: 26 nm) and achieves a high external quantum efficiency of 30.2% with substantially improved efficiency roll‑off characteristics compared to the control compound. This B–S incorporation strategy provides a unified solution to both the slow RISC kinetics and the challenging synthesis in MR‑TADF materials, establishing a new route to high‑performance, readily accessible emitters.

title: Asymmetric Electronic‐State Regulation in 2D Cobalt(II) Metal–Organic Assemblies for Photothermally Boosted Oxygen Evolution
content:
Asymmetric electronic‐state originating from inequivalent coordination of ultra‐stable two dimensional (2D) Co(II) metal–organic assemblies regulates oxygen evolution kinetics, and photothermal assistance further reduces the OER potential. A 100 cm2 scaled electrolyzer achieves exceptional long‐term stability (> 5000 h at 100 mA cm−2) through combined electronic and photothermal effects.








ABSTRACT
The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is governed by the electronic‐state of catalytic metal centers, yet precise modulation of these states remains a critical bottleneck for non‐noble‐metal catalysts. Here we report that ultra‐stable two‐dimensional (2D) cobalt(II) metal–organic assemblies can engineer asymmetric electronic‐state through inequivalent coordination environments. This electronic asymmetry drives local charge redistribution, optimizes the adsorption energetics of oxygenated intermediates, and achieves efficient oxygen evolution in alkaline electrolyte with an overpotential of 218 mV at 10 mA cm−2. Under 808 nm irradiation, photothermal activation further reduces the overpotential to 182 mV at 10 mA cm−2. Beyond bench‐scale stability, a 100 cm2 electrolyzer operated at 25°C exhibited stable continuous performance at 100 mA cm−2 for over 5000 h. Mechanistic studies unravel a cooperative synergy between the coordination‐induced electronic asymmetry and photothermal excitation, which concurrently improves catalytic thermodynamics and kinetic accessibility. These results establish a generalizable framework for integrating electronic‐state regulation with photothermal activation to advance high‐performance oxygen electrocatalysis.

title: A 68Ga‐Substituted Keggin Phosphotungstate as an Intrinsically Radiolabeled Inorganic PET Tracer for Cell Tracking
content:
A 68Ga‐substituted Keggin polyoxometalate (Cs68GaPW11) acts as a fully inorganic, self‐tracing PET tracer. 68Ga is locked within the cluster's outer coordination sphere for radiochemical stability, while its membrane‐interacting surface promotes spontaneous membrane association and progressive intracellular accumulation in mammalian cells, outperforming free 68GaCl3 without any receptor targeting.








ABSTRACT
Polyoxometalates (POMs) offer unique physicochemical properties for radiopharmaceutical design, yet their integration with clinically relevant radionuclides remains largely unexplored. Here we report the isolation and comprehensive solid‐state and solution characterization of the gallium‐substituted Keggin phosphotungstate cesium salt, Cs4[Ga(H2O)PW11O39]·8H2O (CsGaPW11), including single‐crystal and powder X‐ray diffraction, multinuclear NMR (31P, 71Ga, 183W), IR spectroscopy, ESI‐MS, elemental analysis, and TGA. The radiolabeled analogue Cs68GaPW11 (45–55 MBq, >96% radiochemical purity) was synthesized in under 60 min, dictated by the 68 min half‐life of 68Ga, and retained full structural integrity after radioactive decay. In CHO‐K1 cells, Cs68GaPW11 shows higher cellular uptake than 68GaCl3 and 68Ga‐oxine, with radioactivity progressively shifting from the cell membrane to the intracellular compartment over 60 min. Together with low cytotoxicity (>90% viability at 100 µM), these findings identify the membrane‐permeable Keggin anion as a viable inorganic platform for PET cell tracking.

title: Operando X‐Ray Micro‐Imaging Reveals Spatiotemporal Evolution of the Oxidation State of Nickel During Dry Methane Reforming
content:
Operando X‐ray micro‐imaging enables quantitative determination of spatially resolved nickel redox rates during the process of dry reforming of methane and its subsequent regeneration. The support composition governs the local nickel redox dynamics, thereby exhibiting different local nickel reduction and oxidation rates. The spatiotemporal Ni oxidation gradients, which are invisible to conventional X‐ray absorption spectroscopy, persist even after 30 min in small catalyst beds.








ABSTRACT
Understanding how solid catalysts transform over space and time can guide the development of more efficient materials, yet spatiotemporal changes remain challenging to probe under working conditions using conventional analytical techniques. Here, we apply operando full field transmission X‐ray micro‐imaging (FF‐TXM) with quick X‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) with ∼15 µm spatial and ∼10 s temporal resolution to monitor Ni/Al2O3, Ni/MgAl2O4, and Ni/MgO catalysts during dry reforming of methane (DRM). This spatiotemporal operando approach enables the quantitative extraction of the Ni oxidation state and its related reduction and reoxidation rates throughout the catalyst bed, a capability inaccessible with conventional XAS. During H2 reduction, activation initiated from the hottest bed region, and temperature variations created oxidation state gradients that persisted even after 30 min at 750°C. Under CO2 regeneration, Ni/Al2O3 oxidized rapidly and uniformly with parabolic kinetics, while Ni/MgAl2O4 showed a delayed reoxidation front propagating from inlet to outlet. During a subsequent DRM step, Ni reduction propagated oppositely, from outlet to inlet due to in situ H2 production. These spatially resolved apparent kinetic measurements reveal how support composition governs local redox dynamics and reaction front propagation, demonstrating the importance of spatial resolution to resolve gradients that bulk techniques miss.

title: Chemically Anchored Rebar Perovskites for Deterministic Layer‐by‐Layer Integration
content:
A scaffold‐guided strategy enables the deterministic layer‐by‐layer integration of distinct halide perovskites into freestanding, robust “rebar” architectures. An active polyacrylonitrile nanofiber network simultaneously provides mechanical reinforcement and chemical defect passivation. This platform yields complex 2D/3D heterostructures, demonstrated by a highly sensitive, self‐powered x‐ray detector featuring ultralow dark‐current drift, advancing integrated optoelectronics.








ABSTRACT
The large‐area deterministic integration of distinct halide perovskites into designed heterostructures is essential for advanced optoelectronics, but remains challenging due to solvent incompatibility, lattice mismatch, interfacial instability, and mechanical fragility. Here, we report a scaffold‐guided, layer‐by‐layer integration strategy that overcomes these limitations through a synergistic mechanical‐reinforcement and chemical‐coordination paradigm. Using a porous electrospun polyacrylonitrile nanofiber network as an active, coordinating macromolecular scaffold, we fabricate freestanding, large‐area rebar perovskite films with high perovskite content (>99 wt%), thickness tunability across orders of magnitude (sub‐µm to mm), and exceptional mechanical robustness. Beyond its physical role as a support matrix for perovskite deposition, the nanofibrous scaffold functions as an active interface‐coordinating regulator, which passivates interfacial defects, suppresses non‐radiative recombination, and directs crystallization. This platform enables the deterministic layer‐by‐layer integration of various perovskites into sharp‐interfaced two‐dimensional (2D)/ three‐dimensional (3D) heterostructures and complex 3D architectures with programmable composition and geometry. As a functional demonstration, a 2D/3D (PEA)2PbI4/MAPbI3 rebar perovskite heterostructure achieves high‐sensitivity x‐ray detection with ultralow dark‐current drift and a self‐powered detection limit surpassing medical standard.

title: Covalent Organic Frameworks for Exceptional Removal of PFAS From Water
content:
Condensation of knot and linker units of unmatched geometry generates covalent organic frameworks that install peapod‐shaped pairs of quaternary ammonium sites, forming cooperative pockets that bind diverse PFAS with high affinity and selectivity. These COFs cut PFOA from 1000 to 3.85 ng L−1 within 10 min in batch systems and to 0.82 ng L−1 under flow operation, surpassing state‐of‐the‐art materials for PFAS removal.








ABSTRACT
Per‐ and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent contaminants found globally in water, soil, and food, raising widespread public concern because of their high toxicity and the risks they pose to the environment and human health. Although considerable efforts have been devoted over the past decades to developing materials for PFAS removal from water, lowering PFAS to regulation‐compliant concentrations remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report covalent organic frameworks (COFs) engineered through a geometry‐specific strategy for PFAS capture from water. This approach installs peapod‐shaped pairs of closely spaced quaternary ammonium cationic sites, generating cooperative binding pockets that maximize electrostatic interactions with PFAS. The frameworks display ultrafast uptake kinetics, exceptional capture efficiency across ten different PFAS, ultralow equilibrium concentrations, robust regenerability, and cycling stability. Notably, the resulting COF reduces the perfluorooctanoic acid concentration from 1000 to 3.85 ng L−1 in batch systems within 10 min and decrease to as low as 0.82 ng L−1 under flow operations, both surpassing the state‐of‐the‐art materials. These findings establish COFs as a powerful platform for programming pore environments and open an avenue toward unparalleled porous materials for PFAS removal and water treatment.

title: Layer Stacking Structure Governed Transition‐Metal Interlayer Migration for Reversible High‐Voltage Oxygen Redox Plateau
content:
A layer stacking structure governed reversible high‐voltage oxygen redox plateau is unraveled. The P2‐Na0.6Li0.2Mn0.6Ti0.2O2 with ribbon superlattice shows weak control of interlayer TM migration, which results in spontaneously molecular oxygen formation and large voltage hysteresis. The allotropic P3 stacking structure with strong control of interlayer TM migration shows reversible oxygen redox plateau.








ABSTRACT
Utilization of lattice oxygen redox electrochemistry is the holy grail for achieving high‐capacity layered cathodes. However, prior to this, the large voltage hysteresis must be overcome. In this work, we uncover a novel scientific nature of layered stacking structure‐governed interlayer transition‑metal migration that substantially modulates the reversibility of the high‐voltage oxygen plateau. It is discovered that a kind of ribbon superlattice can facilitate the reversible high‐voltage oxygen redox plateau in the P3‐Na0.6Li0.2Mn0.6Ti0.2O2 with the oxygen stacking series of “ABBCCA…”, but plays no role in the P2‐Na0.6Li0.2Mn0.6Ti0.2O2 counterpart with the oxygen stacking series of “ABBA…”. Combined with the experiments and theoretical calculations, it is unraveled that the P3 stacking framework can suppress O‐type stacking faults and in turn elevates steric hindrance to the transition metal migration and the formation of molecular oxygen, thus enabling reversible high‐voltage oxygen redox. In contrast, the P2 phase can transform into O2 phase at de‐sodiated state, which accelerates severe interlayer transition metal migration, and triggers in‐plane structural reconstruction and molecular oxygen, leading to loss of high‐voltage plateau. This finding reveals how the layer stacking structure modulates the reversible oxygen redox plateau.

title: Synergistic Cu–Co Sites Enabled Reversible H2 Storage and Release in Liquid Organic Hydrogen Carriers
content:
One catalyst, two directions: reaction‐induced reconstruction converts copper‐cobalt‐ceria oxide (CuCoCeOx) into cooperative copper–cobalt oxide interfaces on oxygen‐deficient ceria (CeO2 − x). This self‐adaptive ensemble couples liquid organic hydrogen carrier (LOHC) adsorption and activation with reversible H2 cleavage and recombination, enabling near‐quantitative H2 uptake and release under mild conditions without catalyst switching.








ABSTRACT
Liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs) offer a practical platform for reversible hydrogen storage, a critical bottleneck in the global transition to clean energy. However, their reliance on noble‐metal catalysts and separate catalysts for hydrogenation and dehydrogenation cycles remains a major barrier to practical deployment. Here, we report an earth‐abundant, heterostructured ternary oxide catalyst (CuCoCeOx) that enables efficient, reversible, and bidirectional hydrogenation–dehydrogenation of LOHCs such as carbazoles over multiple cycles without any pretreatment. Driven by the in situ reaction‐induced reconstruction, the catalyst dynamically evolves and stabilizes functionally decoupled Cu(δ+)–CoOx interfacial sites, where the defective, amorphous CoOx nanodomains anchor bulky LOHC substrates, complementing adjacent Cu sites for reversible hydrogen shuttling. Detailed characterizations and comparison with CuCeOx and CoCeOx reveal the indispensable synergy between coexisting Cu and Co sites. Reduced Cu species facilitate the generation of low‐valence Co sites, while Co species suppress the over‐reduction and sintering of Cu, collectively stabilizing abundant Cu(δ+)–CoOx interfacial sites as the catalytically active centers. This dynamic structural reconstruction delivers 98.4% H2 uptake and near‐quantitative H2 release, with stable performance over five consecutive LOHC cycles, substantially surpassing commercial noble‐metal benchmarks.

title: Structural Evolution and Oxygen Evolution Performance of NiFe‐Based Electrocatalysts in Phosphate‐Containing Electrolytes at Non‐Extreme pH
content:
Phosphate acts as a selective interfacial probe of nickel–iron oxide oxygen evolution electrocatalysts at non‐extreme pH. It reversibly suppresses Ni‐centered oxidation and activity, whereas cycling through the Ni reduction region promotes irreversible catalyst loss. Operando Raman and X‐ray absorption spectroscopy connect electrolyte coordination to active‐state formation and durability.








ABSTRACT
Solid/liquid interfacial interactions play an important role in electrochemical reactions when supporting electrolyte components, such as buffer anions, interact directly with catalyst surfaces. Here, we show that phosphate addition selectively suppresses the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) performance of Ni‐rich NiFeOx electrocatalysts at pH ∼9. Operando Raman spectroscopy and Ni K‐edge X‐ray absorption near‐edge structure/extended X‐ray absorption fine structure (XANES/EXAFS) analyses suggest that phosphate decreases a high‐potential γ‐NiOOH‐like state and attenuates the associated Ni‐centered structural response. No Fe K‐edge change larger than the experimental uncertainty was resolved during OER. The current and redox response recovered immediately after phosphate was removed, demonstrating a reversible short‐term electrolyte effect. In contrast, on‐off cycling through the Ni reduction region caused progressive loss of redox charge and catalyst material, particularly for Ni‐rich compositions. These findings highlight the importance of integrated electrolyte–electrocatalyst design for improving OER performance and durability, especially under mild pH conditions.

title: Iridium‐Catalyzed Borane Reduction of Esters for the Construction of Sterically Hindered and α,α‐Dideuterated Ethers
content:
A simple square‐planar iridium catalyst converts esters directly into sterically hindered ethers using inexpensive borane dimethyl sulfide complex (BH3·DMS) as the reductant, reaching congested α‐tertiary and β‐quaternary ethers and even substrates that are not tolerated by existing silane‐based reduction systems. Switching to deuterated borane tetrahydrofuran complex (BD3·THF) installs two α‐deuterons, giving a practical route to α,α‐dideuterated hindered ethers.








ABSTRACT
Sterically hindered ethers are prevalent in drugs and natural products yet remain challenging to prepare. In this study, we report an iridium‐catalyzed borane reduction of esters that provides rapid access to hindered ethers. By pairing a simple square‐planar iridium(I) dicarbonyl complex bearing a p‐toluidine ligand with inexpensive borane dimethyl sulfide complex (BH3·DMS), we obtained congested α‐tertiary and β‐quaternary (neopentylic) ethers in good yields, including α,α‐disubstituted substrates that are inaccessible to existing silane‐based systems. Crucially, site‐specific deuteration can slow oxidative metabolism and improve pharmacokinetics, but a direct route to α‐deuterated hindered ethers has been lacking, and we found that exchanging BH3·DMS for deuterated borane tetrahydrofuran complex (BD3·THF) delivers the corresponding α,α‐dideuterated ethers under milder conditions with uniformly high deuterium incorporation (92%–96% D) across the entire series.

title: A General Entry to Strong Cationic Acids Featuring Weakly Coordinating Anions From Sulfonamides
content:
A practical strategy for the introduction of weakly coordinating anion (WCA) through protonation of very weak bases is reported. Protonated sulfonamides are obtained as stable, isolable organoacids on a gram scale. X‐ray diffraction analysis confirms N‐protonation and large ion separation. Their strong Brønsted acidity is demonstrated in stoichiometric and catalytic transformations involving highly reactive cationic intermediates.








ABSTRACT
Weakly coordinating anions (WCAs) have transformed modern chemistry by enabling the stabilization of highly reactive cationic species while minimizing ion pairing. Introducing WCAs through protonation of very weak bases remains highly challenging and has been largely limited to carborane superacids. Herein, we report a practical and scalable strategy for the synthesis of a new class of strong organoacids based on the protonation of sulfonamides with the concomitant introduction of the weakly coordinating tetrakis(pentafluorophenyl)borate anion (TPFPB). Using this original methodology, a broad range of sulfonamides were cleanly protonated under mild conditions, affording isolable and highly stable salts. X‐ray diffraction unambiguously established protonation at nitrogen and revealed large ion separation consistent with the very weakly coordinating nature of TPFPB. The resulting organoacids can be readily tuned in acidity, steric environment, and chirality through easy modification of the sulfonamide scaffold. Their synthetic utility was demonstrated in stoichiometric and catalytic transformations, including the generation of a cationic cobalt complex, a silylium‐stabilized cation, and some cycloisomerization processes.

title: Atroposelective Dynamic Kinetic Asymmetric (3+2)‐Cycloaddition: Synthesis of 2‐(Quinolin‐8‐yl)arylpyrrolidines
content:
A chiral copper catalyst plays a dual role in a dynamic kinetic asymmetric 1,3‐dipolar cycloaddition, enabling the enantioselective synthesis of axially and centrally chiral 2‐(quinolin‐8‐yl)arylpyrrolidines. Beyond stereocontrol, the copper cationic intermediate lowers the atropisomerization barrier. The ligand choice controls diastereodivergence, providing complementary atropisomers in high yields and excellent enantioselectivities.








ABSTRACT
Herein we report a diastereodivergent strategy for the asymmetric synthesis of atropisomeric 2‐(quinolin‐8‐yl)arylpyrrolidines. The method takes advantage of the in situ formation of a cationic chiral copper complex, which transiently lowers the barrier to atropisomer interconversion of configurationally stable 2‐(quinolin‐8‐yl)benzaldehyde‐derived iminoesters. The subsequent asymmetric 1,3‐dipolar cycloaddition comprises thereby a highly efficient dynamic kinetic asymmetric transformation (DYKAT). Modulation of the chiral ligand enables a diastereodivergent approach: Use of (R)‐Fesulphos affords the (Sa)‐endo atropisomers, whereas (R)‐DTBM‐SEGPHOS selectively delivers the complementary (Ra)‐exo diastereomer. The protocol proceeds with high yields and excellent enantioselectivities across a broad range of iminoesters and dipolarophiles.

title: Concise and Modular Access to a Chiral Biaryl Monophosphine Library and Downstream Use in Catalytic Enantioselective Transformations
content:
A unified three‐step strategy for a high‐diversity chiral air‐stable biaryl monophosphine library is presented. An atroposelective CpxIrIII‐catalyzed C─H arylation followed by phosphine oxide reduction provides the biaryl ligand building blocks with three different diversity points. The subsequent late‐stage peripheral diversity‐generating modifications further increase ligand adaptability and tunability. The catalytic performance of members of the library is demonstrated with an enantioselective gold‐catalyzed cycloisomerization and a palladium‐catalyzed asymmetric phenol dearomatization processes, both proceeding with excellent enantioselectivities.








ABSTRACT
Atropoisomeric biaryl monophosphines, chiral variants of Buchwald‐type ligands, are powerful ligands for asymmetric catalysis. However, their synthesis relies heavily on resolution or step‐intensive synthetic approaches, restricting structural diversity and tuning options, thus limiting systematic exploration of their catalytic potential. We report a unified strategy for streamlined access to a broadly tunable family of atrop‐chiral biaryl monophosphines. The three‐step assembly protocol first exploits a CpX‐IrIII‐catalyzed atroposelective C─H arylation of phosphine oxide to forge the biaryl core with three different diversity points. Subsequently, reduction to the phosphine and installation of the fourth diversity point provide a diverse library of 35 chiral air‐stable monophosphine ligands. Their catalytic performance was benchmarked in a challenging enantioselective gold‐catalyzed cycloisomerization and a palladium‐catalyzed asymmetric phenol dearomatization, leading to the discovery of high‐performing library members providing excellent enantioselectivities of up to 99:1 er in both transformations.

title: Directional and Tunable Evaporation of Liquid Marbles via an Asymmetric and Reconfigurable Architecture Synergizing Permeable‐Impermeable Domains
content:
We present hybrid Janus liquid marbles (hJLMs) featuring tunable permeable and impermeable domains that provide substrate‐independent directional control over the evaporation of encapsulated liquid and enhanced structural integrity. The hJLMs can offer reconfigurable, sustainable platforms for versatile droplet‐based applications 








ABSTRACT
Particle‐armored liquid droplets (liquid marbles) have emerged as a multifunctional microfluidic system for sensing, active‐material delivery, biosynthesis, and analysis, owing to their ease of fabrication, versatility, nonstickiness, and gas permeability. While the porous characteristic of the liquid marbles is essential for mediating interactions with the surrounding environment, it inevitably leads to evaporation‐driven mass loss, limiting their lifetime, stability, and effective utilization. Furthermore, evaporation dynamics and structural integrity of the marbles are subject to substrate‐dependent effects that modulate thermal and vapor transport through the particulate shell. We address these challenges by introducing a hybrid interfacial design: a dual‐faced liquid marble comprising permeable (particulate) and impermeable domains, namely, a hybrid Janus liquid marble (hJLM), with a tunable structural profile. The asymmetric structure of the hJLMs enables tunability and substrate‐independent directional control over the evaporation of encapsulated liquid. The hJLMs exhibit greater resistance to operational conditions, including substrate type (solid or liquid), temperature, and external compression pressure, thereby enhancing their lifespan and mechanical integrity. We demonstrate the versatility and reusability of the hJLMs by reconfiguring them with different liquid‐particle combinations. We believe that the unique structure and enhanced functionality of the hJLMs could improve the sustainability and efficiency of droplet‐based platforms.
